entries.note: He reports his own growing concerns; the proposition turns that personal assessment into an objective condition.

entries.test: Contemporaneous financial reporting and the basis of the investors' projections would establish whether the reported figures were fabricated or unsupported.
entries.note: Calling the promotional statement fictional does not clearly commit him to a specific year-end revenue forecast. His accusation is his own, although the figures originate with investors.
The source judges one paragraph and its exclusive purpose; the proposition broadens this to Reuters coverage. 'Questionable economics' is evaluative.

entries.test: Annual financial disclosures or credible financial reporting would establish Anthropic's losses and the profitability of the AI labs discussed.
Anthropic's quarterly accounts and the documented value of the May–June compute discounts would show whether profit depended on those discounts.
entries.note: This is an accounting dependency that can be tested from actual costs and concessions.
'I cannot see a viable (or reasonable) path' is weaker than declaring that no path will exist. Viability or reasonableness has no agreed test here.

entries.test: Anthropic's eventual S-1 would show whether its disclosed finances feature substantial losses, cash burn and onerous commitments.
entries.note: The surrounding financial discussion supplies a plain meaning for the metaphor.

entries.test: Comparative financial disclosures and spending on the named side projects would test whether avoiding those projects contributes to Anthropic's stronger financial condition.
entries.note: The claim includes an explicit causal explanation.
'Hard to imagine' expresses doubt rather than a firm outcome.

entries.test: OpenAI's 2025 financial statements or credible reporting of them would establish its revenue and loss.

entries.note: 'A real problem' does not specify an outcome or a shared threshold for seriousness.

entries.test: Successive revenue figures and scheduled financial obligations would show whether growth decelerated while funding requirements increased.
OpenAI's 2025 revenue records and customer revenue breakdown would establish the total and SoftBank's contribution.
OpenAI's run-rate calculation dates and underlying weekly revenue would show whether it selects unusually busy four-week windows that overstate representative revenue.

entries.note: The proposition drops the exclusive 'only' from the marketing claim. The judgment of usefulness should be separated from the factual assertion about recurring token revenue.

entries.test: Dated run-rate announcements would establish OpenAI's projected $40 billion figure and Anthropic's reported $65 billion July figure.
entries.note: The source says OpenAI was 'on track' to reach $40 billion, not that it had already reached that run rate.
This attributes a private motive for promoting the metric.

entries.test: OpenAI's Q1 2026 revenue and compute expense records would establish the stated $6.4 billion shortfall before other expenses.
Revenue, usage and service-cost data across periods would show whether increased revenue brings increased service costs.

entries.note: This is an overall judgment without identifying which particular commitments are impossible.

entries.test: Compute contracts, payment schedules and equity-payment provisions would establish the demand and funding requirements for satisfying OpenAI's obligations.
OpenAI's annual fundraising, continued operations and profitability through approximately 2030 would test the asserted survival requirement.
entries.note: Survival with materially less funding would contradict the claimed necessity.

entries.test: Comparative growth and enterprise customer figures, together with any OpenAI IPO filings, would test the comparison and the asserted IPO prerequisite.
entries.note: The record combines present comparisons with a future IPO prerequisite.

entries.test: OpenAI's revenue through 2030 and its survival, IPO and fulfillment of obligations would test whether roughly tenfold growth was necessary.

entries.note: 'Anything in modern history' is sweeping exaggeration without a comparable financial measure.

entries.test: Anthropic's contractual commitments through August 2029 and both companies' financial results would establish its obligations and comparable unprofitability.
entries.note: 'Similarly unprofitable' does not assert an equal degree of unprofitability.
The forecast explicitly says 'unlikely'; the historical catch-up assertion is separately testable.

entries.test: Following revenue acceleration, OpenAI's costs, financing needs and funding rounds would show whether several additional rounds around $122 billion were required.
entries.note: The proposition drops the antecedent of accelerating revenue and substitutes the broader relationship between revenue and costs.

entries.test: SoftBank's liquidity disclosures, debt documents and investment capacity would establish the collateralized loan and its ability to fund further OpenAI investment.
OpenAI's annual financing requirements would show whether each year requires more than its latest requested funding round.
entries.note: 'Last asked for' is not 'raised the previous time'; the latter also introduces a rolling comparison.

entries.test: OpenAI's eventual liquidity failure or sustained financial self-sufficiency, alongside its corporate scale, would test the stated alternatives.
entries.note: The preceding alternative supplies the exception, making this conditional.

entries.test: OpenAI's existing contracts and payment schedules would establish whether at least $800 billion is required over the stated period.
entries.note: Existing obligations can be checked before their payment deadlines.

entries.test: Payment schedules, cash-flow disclosures and fundraising through December 2027 would show whether the obligations required another massive funding round.
Delivered hyperscaler capacity and OpenAI's resulting contractual compute payments through December 2027 would test the $147 billion requirement.

entries.note: 'Almost certainly' states a probability, and the size and IPO timing are also explicitly qualified.

entries.test: OpenAI's quarterly compute expenses would establish whether they exceed $12 billion.
Funding-round composition, documented fundraising attempts and major backers' liquidity disclosures would establish dependence on large, financially strained backers.
The Ohio project's guarantee terms would establish whether NVIDIA covers completed assets rather than OpenAI's ongoing lease payments.
Private credit commitments and documented financing capacity would show whether those funds can supply OpenAI more than $100 billion annually.
entries.note: 'Could stomach' expresses a firm capacity limit here, not a possibility forecast.

entries.test: Public reporting on delayed, failed or undersubscribed private credit deals for AI data centers would establish financing difficulties.
If data-center financing difficulties persist, documented OpenAI private credit fundraising attempts would show whether attracting investors also proves substantially difficult.
entries.note: The proposition turns 'if' into 'since' and adds an explicit comparative 'much more'.

entries.test: Historical funding-round disclosures and investor classifications would establish whether either company raised more than $30 billion in venture capital in a single round.
entries.note: 'Scraped the bottom of the barrel' does not literally establish that venture capital was exhausted.
The proposition broadens these companies and deals to AI labs generally. The investor-liquidity premise is explicitly 'very unlikely'.

entries.test: OpenAI's funding history and investor allocations would establish total funding from investors other than the four named companies.
Venture funding commitments and documented fundraising delays or shortfalls would establish the difficulty of mobilizing more than a few billion dollars for OpenAI.
OpenAI's annual financing and continued solvency would show whether it can survive a year with less than $100 billion in new funding.

entries.note: He explicitly introduces this explanation as a guess.

entries.test: OpenAI's cash-flow statements and compute prepayment schedules would establish its recurring funding needs and their relationship to growth.
entries.note: The record combines a current funding requirement with its asserted growth relationship.

entries.test: A future inability to meet major payment obligations or raise replacement funds, followed by OpenAI's operational outcome, would test the forecast.
entries.note: The payment and funding failure is an explicit antecedent.

entries.test: OpenAI's Q1 2026 cash-flow reconciliation would establish whether financing inflows alone explain the improvement in its cash position.
entries.note: 'Only by virtue of' explicitly attributes the improvement to a cause.

entries.test: OpenAI's liquidity, scheduled payments and financing through November 18, 2026 would establish whether it needed additional money within three months.
entries.note: The core need for money is firm; its amount is qualified. The proposition makes upfront capacity payments definite where the source calls them likely.

entries.test: OpenAI's cost trends, pricing changes, enterprise customer responses and financing requirements would test the asserted link between growth and continued fundraising.
entries.note: 'No clear path' is weaker than an absolute inability to cut costs or raise prices.

entries.test: OpenAI's unit costs at different scales, operating losses and dependence on external financing would test the stated financial characteristics.
Subsequent fundraising timelines, shortfalls, concessions and investor participation would show whether securing additional capital proves difficult.

entries.note: The historical superlative is hyperbole without a defined economic measure.

entries.test: Successive comparable revenue figures for OpenAI and Anthropic would establish their growth trends and relative pace.
OpenAI's cash balances, obligations and financing through December 31, 2026 would establish whether it needed additional money.
entries.note: The need for money is firm; only the estimated amount is qualified.

entries.test: A documented cash-payment default involving a creditor unwilling to accept equity or IOUs would establish the predicted event.
OpenAI's run rate by November 18, 2026 and its competitive revenue position against Anthropic would test the asserted $60 billion prerequisite.
entries.note: This states a competitive requirement, not a prediction that the target will be met.

entries.test: OpenAI's run rate through November 18, 2026 and the sequence of any ensuing financial distress would show whether a missed target or revenue regression was the first deterioration.
entries.note: The passage's general speculation disclaimer does not remove this specific firm prediction.

entries.test: Both companies' revenue growth and corporate token-maxxing spending through year-end 2026 would test the predicted slowdown and expiration of those initiatives.
entries.note: Only token-maxxing initiatives are said to peter out by year-end. The proposition also applies that deadline to subsidized subscriptions.

entries.test: Fable adoption data, customer price responses and the discussed companies' subsequent pricing outcomes would test whether price sensitivity prevents effective price increases.
entries.note: The proposition generalizes a discussion of Anthropic and OpenAI to AI labs broadly. The source attributes limited pricing power to price-sensitive adoption.
The proposed motive is expressly speculative.
The proposition omits the preceding September timing. 'Defend itself against economics' has no shared decisive test.

entries.test: Documented nonpayment of an amount owed by OpenAI to a counterparty would establish the predicted interruption.
An announced or documented subsequent OpenAI fundraising round would settle the firm expectation of another fundraise.
entries.note: 'Heavily funded by' does not mean 'led by'. Asset-manager participation and NVIDIA's return remain qualified details.

entries.test: Provider-level compute demand and customer concentration disclosures would establish whether OpenAI represents a majority at effectively every provider.
entries.note: The majority-demand assertion is firm and checkable; the appended prediction of support is probabilistic.
'Increasingly confident' is changed to 'likely'. The predicted act of privately considering an IPO cannot itself be settled by public evidence.
The proposition replaces the alleged swindling mechanism with enterprise business size. 'Desperate and untenable' and 'no clear way out' lack a common decisive test.

entries.test: Altman's public statements during material OpenAI financial distress would show whether he invokes future-building challenges and blames critics.
entries.note: The rest of the paragraph supports the added reference to blaming critics.

entries.test: Government appropriations, agreements and subsequent disclosures would establish whether a $150 billion bailout arrangement existed at publication.
entries.note: A supposedly secret financial arrangement can be established or disproved through public disclosures.

entries.test: Following a Microsoft absorption of OpenAI, initial contract decisions and revised Azure guidance would show whether nearly all cloud contracts were canceled and $250 billion removed.
entries.note: The proposition omits the material sequencing claim that cancellation would be Microsoft's first move.
Free-product cuts are merely 'potential'; the proposition strengthens them to 'likely'.
'I imagine some rescue package' does not explicitly rank rescue as more likely than failure. It also omits the source's broader consequences for other dependent companies.

entries.test: Nadella's investor statements compared with Microsoft's actual AI customer revenue concentration would show whether those statements were misleading.
entries.note: This can be assessed as a claim about representations without proving private intent.

entries.test: Hyperscaler revenue disclosures after OpenAI's failure and Microsoft's customer concentration data would test the predicted material revenue decline and the 70% premise.
Anthropic's financial results and eventual fulfillment or default on its hundreds of billions in commitments would test the assertion.
entries.note: The claim about promises it cannot keep predicts future nonperformance, alongside a present profitability comparison.
The merger prediction is explicitly probabilistic; the conditional harm claim could be extracted separately.

entries.test: OpenAI's Q1 2026 non-GAAP operating results would establish whether its operating margin was negative 122%.
OpenAI's year-end 2026 run rate and subsequent payment of its compute obligations would test whether roughly $75 billion was a necessary threshold.
entries.note: The 'chance' idiom expresses a firm necessary condition here.

entries.test: OpenAI's eventual failure and unpaid counterparty claims would establish the predicted collapse and defaults.
Following OpenAI's collapse, SoftBank's solvency disclosures and major counterparties' guidance revisions would show whether the predicted consequences occurred.
OpenAI's scheduled cloud commitments compared with hyperscalers' contemporaneous projected cloud revenues would establish whether the share is at least 20%.
entries.note: The 20% floor is firm; the higher range is qualified. The source presents a current comparison of commitments and projected revenues.

entries.test: OpenAI's annual revenue and fulfillment of more than $800 billion in obligations over the stated three-year period would test his declared conditions for being wrong.
entries.note: The source states requirements for falsifying his thesis, rather than explicitly forecasting that this conjunction will not occur. Its three-year wording also sits awkwardly with the cited 2030 projection.

entries.test: Documented creditor losses, investment write-downs and counterparty revenue declines following OpenAI's collapse would establish economic consequences.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion identifies concrete forms of damage.
The surrounding passage supplies the condition of OpenAI's collapse.
'Vast majority' is weakened to 'most', and unwillingness to contemplate the risk becomes an assertion about people's probability estimates.

entries.test: If Oracle loses OpenAI's revenue, its subsequent solvency and continued operations would establish whether it collapses.
Documented losses and disruption following an OpenAI collapse would establish whether the collapse causes unavoidable damage.
entries.note: This sentence asserts damage from a collapse; the proposition adds an independent assertion that collapse will occur.

entries.test: Compute contracts, supplier equity investments and independent paying-customer demand would test whether apparent AI demand was generated by circular financing rather than underlying customer spending.
entries.note: The proposition captures a causal claim about how apparent demand was created.
